title: In Luke 21 How Can We As Believers Prepare For Trials While Awaiting His Return
paragraphs: Understanding Luke 21: Preparing for Trials While Awaiting Christ’s Return

Luke 21 stands as one of the most profound chapters where Jesus addresses His disciples about the coming trials, the destruction of Jerusalem, and ultimately, His return. The teaching is not just prophetic, but intensely practical for every believer living in anticipation of Christ’s second coming. In this study, we will explore how Jesus equips His followers to face trials with courage, faith, and steadfastness.
1. The Context: Jesus Foretells Difficult Days

Jesus’ words in Luke 21 are spoken as He observes people in the temple and responds to questions about the future. He warns of coming persecutions, wars, natural disasters, and cosmic disturbances. Yet, His purpose is not to incite fear, but to encourage preparedness and unwavering trust in God.
And when ye shall hear of wars and tumults, be not terrified: for these things must needs come to pass first; but the end is not immediately. - Luke 21:9 ASV
2. Watchfulness and Spiritual Alertness

One of Jesus’ central exhortations is for believers to “watch” and pray. This watchfulness is not passive waiting but an active, daily readiness, marked by discernment and prayerful dependence on God.

But take heed to yourselves, lest haply your hearts be overcharged with surfeiting, and drunkenness, and cares of this life, and that day come on you suddenly as a snare: for so shall it come upon all them that dwell on the face of all the earth. But watch ye at every season, making supplication, that ye may prevail to escape all these things that shall come to pass, and to stand before the Son of man. - Luke 21:34-36 ASV
Jesus warns against being weighed down by the distractions and anxieties of life. Instead, He urges believers to cultivate a lifestyle of prayer and vigilance, staying spiritually alert to the times.
3. Endurance Through Trials
A key theme in Luke 21 is endurance. Jesus assures His disciples that persecution and hardship will come, but He promises His sustaining presence and the gift of the Holy Spirit to empower them.

Settle it therefore in your hearts, not to meditate beforehand how to answer: for I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to withstand or to gainsay. - Luke 21:14-15 ASV

This promise is a reminder that God equips His people for whatever trials they will face. Believers are not left to their own strength, but are provided with divine wisdom and courage to bear testimony to Christ.
4. The Example of Faithfulness

The chapter begins with the story of a poor widow who gives all she has to God (Luke 21:1-4). Her simple act of faith and trust is set before us as a model for how to live with open hands, even in uncertain times:

And he said, Of a truth I say unto you, This poor widow cast in more than they all: for all these did of their superfluity cast in unto the gifts; but she of her want did cast in all the living that she had. - Luke 21:3-4 ASV
Her example encourages us to trust God fully, giving ourselves to Him without reservation, even when circumstances seem dire.
5. The Hope of His Return

Amidst warnings and calls to vigilance, Jesus anchors our hope in His triumphant return. No matter how severe the tribulations, believers are to look up with confidence, knowing redemption is drawing near.

And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory. But when these things begin to come to pass, look up, and lift up your heads; because your redemption draweth nigh. - Luke 21:27-28 ASV
This hope is central: the trials of this world are temporary, but the coming of Christ is sure.
6. Practical Steps for Preparation
Abide in the Word: Daily immersion in Scripture strengthens faith and helps discern truth from deception (Psalm 119:105 ASV).
Persistent Prayer: Maintaining a continual conversation with God keeps believers spiritually alert (1 Thessalonians 5:17 ASV).
Active Fellowship: Encouraging and supporting one another in the body of Christ is vital (Hebrews 10:24-25 ASV).
Hope in Christ: Fixing our eyes on Jesus and the promise of His return sustains us through adversity (Titus 2:13 ASV).
Conclusion

Luke 21 calls every believer to a life of watchful faith, resilient endurance, and unwavering hope as we await Christ’s return. Our preparation is not found in stockpiling resources or retreating in fear, but in steadfast devotion to Jesus, empowered by His Spirit and grounded in His Word. The assurance of His presence and the certainty of His coming fill us with courage to endure whatever trials may come, knowing that our ultimate redemption is near.
